newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIAN C.BANK GOVERNOR SEES BANKING SECTOR RECOVERY.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIAN C.BANK GOVERNOR SEES BANKING SECTOR RECOVERY.

text.p: Lithuania's central bank said on Tuesday that the country's banking sector is recovering from a crisis and that tougher supervision policies were yielding positive results.

"During the last year we have been restoring the (people's) trust in commercial banks and this process continues," the governor of the Bank of Lithuania, Reinoldijus Sharkinas, said in an address to parliament.
He said that bad loans were being weeded out of the sector as banks become more discerning in their creidt policies.
"The credit policies of the commercial banks are moving in a positive direction," Sharkinas said.
Sharkinas also said that international accounting standards were applied by all the banks and that audits will be introduced gradually to the whole sector.
He said that the central bank aims at tightening its supervision to avoid a repeat of the crisis that rocked the sector in late 1995 with the shock closure of two of the country's largest banks.
"We intend to inspect every bank each year," Sharkinas added.
